verdict.rationale: Both changes make the same core fix: wrong values are collected and reported together, unknown keys and missing files are refused, upstream.url is validated, and Main exits with status 2. B is slightly ahead on the details. Its unknown-key error lists the valid keys, its duration overflow error is accurate, and its tests pin the exact messages plus the overflow and token-not-echoed cases. Both reports are accurate (17 and 19 test counts check out), and B's adds the actual output and the open choices for the developer to confirm.
a_issues: Duration overflow is reported as a format error ('must be a whole number followed by ms, s or m') even though the value is well-formed, which is misleading.
The unknown-key error does not suggest the valid keys, so the deployer has to look them up to fix a typo.
Fewer edge-case tests: no overflow test, and no test that the API token is kept out of error messages.
b_issues: The out-of-range and not-a-number cases share one message ('must be a whole number, at least N'), which is a little less precise.
The unknown-key message repeats the full list of known keys for every unknown key, which gets noisy when there are several typos.
The report is long relative to a change of this size.

verdict.rationale: Both changes do essentially the same work: they collect every problem, reject invalid present values, unknown keys and missing files, and exit with status 2 from Main. A's error messages help the deployer more, because unknown-key errors list the valid keys and an overflowing timeout is reported as too large rather than as a format error. A also tests more edge cases, including the overflow and a check that the API token is never echoed. B's main advantage is cleaner reuse of required() for upstream.url.
a_issues: uri() repeats the required-check logic instead of calling required().
intValue uses one message for both non-numeric and below-minimum values, which is slightly less precise.
b_issues: An overflowing timeout such as 99999999999999999999m gets the generic format message, which is misleading.
The unknown-key error does not list the valid keys, so the deployer has to look them up.
There is no test for the overflow case and no test that the API token is never echoed.
